Hi <@U04G02LPZ6W>! Have a story update and an ask.

• I’ve found the perfect character to round out our story. His name is Lino, he lives in LA and started his own peptides company. He went from broke just 16 months ago to now doing over $200,000/month in revenue. He imports peptides from China and then sells them with the help of fitness influencers (like Hunter in Arkansas — so flows nicely from what we already have).
• On top of that he’s now started a business teaching others how to break into the peptides industry. He’s trying to get into the “info space,” which is this world of young hustlers teaching other guys how to get rich quick. That in itself seems like a lucrative business to him.
• And this is where I think we’ll do truly original, exclusive reporting on peptides. Everyone’s covering what they are, and how they’re being sold on the gray market, but no other outlets are really exposing the crazy business model underlying the peptides boom. 
• You have “affiliates” at the bottom (who themselves can make tens of thousands a month on commission), company owners above them, then the “gurus” selling peptides business courses at the top. 
• Peptide companies aren’t just selling the idea of a perfect body, they’re also selling the fantasy getting rich off the gray market. Also, I think it’s just a matter of time until someone gets really hurt.
